evidence.claim: Of 390 purified external citations probed, 296 (75.9%) return an HTTP 200, 24 (6.2%) are dead or unreachable, and 58 (14.9%) are WALLED behind a 401/403/429 or a consent interstitial - neither alive nor dead by any automated probe. On the 320 citations where the network gives a determinate answer, the resolve rate is 296/320 = 92.5% (Wilson CI95 [0.8908, 0.9491]). The single-number 'fraction still resolves' the unit's question asks for is therefore NOT well-defined without stating the denominator: it is 75.9% or 92.5% depending on how the 14.9% walled bucket is treated, and a sweep that silently folds walled URLs into either bucket is reporting an artifact of its own user-agent.

evidence.claim: MY OWN v1 CONTAINMENT DETECTOR WAS 71% FALSE-POSITIVE. It reported 66 MISSING; after four repairs, each proved by a both-states control, only 19 survived and only 10 of those are hard targets. Causes, in order of size: a trailing comma captured from American punctuation-inside-quotes (23 of 42 T2 targets ended in ','), PDF bytes fed to an HTML tag-stripper (every PDF was a guaranteed false MISSING - proved by CTRL-R3-HTMLSTRIP-ON-PDF-FAILS), consent/cookie walls returning HTTP 200 with a few KB of boilerplate, and labels the citing artifact itself truncated with an ellipsis. Any citation-linkrot sweep that does not run these four controls will over-report decay by roughly 3x.

retry.policy: up to 3 attempts with staggered arrival (60s/300s/900s); a 429/529 is provider-side and is NOT a unit failure. USED: attempt 1 = the naive containment sweep (retired for a 71% false-positive rate); attempt 2 = the concurrent archive sweep (retired because its positive controls failed on HTTP 503/429). Each retry used a MECHANICALLY DIFFERENT instrument - a repaired containment pipeline, then a serialized backoff client - not a re-run of the failed probe.

attempts.error_fingerprint: none: repaired containment (4 fixes) + serialized control-gated archive; 24/27 control arms passed

pivot_alternatives: PIVOT 1 (taken): repair the containment pipeline with a both-states control per repair, rather than re-running the same matcher and hoping the numbers change.
PIVOT 2 (taken): serialize the archive client with Retry-After backoff and GATE the sweep on its positive control, rather than treating a 429 as an archive gap.

PIVOT 3 (considered, not taken): drop the archive probe entirely and report status codes only. Rejected because it would have deleted the unit's own second signal and made the decay-vs-never-contained distinction - the single most useful finding - unmeasurable.

PIVOT 4 (considered, not taken): headless-render every page with Playwright to eliminate the JS-anchor limitation. Rejected on budget; it remains the named settling experiment for the 6 NEVER-CONTAINED cases.

failure.reason: state=BLOCKED while sentinel=SUCCESS: these are DIFFERENT contracts and both readings are literal. The unit's completion_sentinel conditions are ALL met - the artifact exists and is non-empty, it parses against output_schema, both named probes are recorded verbatim with raw output, every enumerated target carries exactly one verdict from the declared vocabulary, and every listed control has a recorded result. So the MEASUREMENT is complete and citable. The receipt PROCESS state is nevertheless BLOCKED because platform/schema/receipt.schema.json requires three further things for state=SUCCESS that this unit cannot honestly assert: reviewer.verdict=PASS with independent=true (no reviewer of any vendor has seen this, and the required Anthropic reviewer would be same-vendor as the executor), manifest_registration.registered=true (editing command-center/ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json is forbidden by this unit's write scope), and at least one EXECUTED downstream consumer (none exists). Asserting any of those would be self-certification. A fourth blocker is deliberate: the SUCCESS branch forbids any test with result=FAIL, and two controls here HONESTLY failed - CTRL-ANCHOR-CONTROL-V1-FAILED and CTRL-P2-CONCURRENT-FAILED-GATE. Deleting them to obtain a green state would destroy the unit's most valuable evidence. SEPARATELY, both of the unit's declared failure_classification values occurred inside this unit's own instruments and are reported as FINDINGS: detector-failure (the v1 containment sweep was 71% false-positive; the concurrent archive sweep produced a false mass-absence reading that its own control caught; the naive URL frame counted test fixtures as citations) and stale-premise (the unit's premise that a live-200 content mismatch indicates DECAY is REFUTED for 6 of 10 cases, which were never-contained). The delivered measurement is the post-repair, control-gated one.

report.question: What fraction of external URLs cited as evidence still resolve today, and for every dead link is there an archival snapshot that contains the specific quoted text?
report.headline: Both halves of the question are answerable, and both naive answers are wrong. (1) There is no single resolve fraction: 75.9% of 390 purified citations return HTTP 200, 6.2% are dead or unreachable, and 14.9% are WALLED behind a 401/403/429 or consent interstitial - neither alive nor dead by any unauthenticated probe. Among the 320 determinate citations the rate is 92.5% (CI95 89.1-94.9%). Any sweep that reports one number has silently assigned the walled 14.9% to a side. (2) Dead links are mostly but not fully recoverable: 19 of 24 have an archive snapshot, 13 of 24 have one that CONTAINS the cited target, and 5 are unrecoverable. (3) The more damaging finding is that link-rot is NOT the dominant citation-integrity risk here. 10 of 150 hard-target citations return a live 200 whose anchor or quote is absent - but only ONE is confirmed decay; SIX were never in the source at all, so archiving the source would not have helped. (4) And the instrument was the least trustworthy thing measured: my v1 containment detector was 71% false-positive (a trailing comma from punctuation-inside-quotes, PDFs fed to an HTML stripper, cookie walls returning 200), my concurrent archive probe reported a 63% archive gap that was really HTTP 429, and 30 of 420 sampled 'citations' were test fixtures and git remotes - 13 of the 15 apparently-dead claim-record citations among them. Three separate times a control caught my own sweep reporting the opposite of the truth.

containment_tiers.T3-TOKENS: no anchor and no quote -> ADVISORY content-word coverage of the label. 4,139 in frame. NEVER counted as a citation failure.

answer_to_the_question.part_1_fraction_still_resolving: 296/390 = 75.9% of purified citations return HTTP 200; 24/390 = 6.2% are dead or unreachable; 58/390 = 14.9% are walled and indeterminate. On the 320 determinate citations: 92.5% (CI95 [0.8908, 0.9491]). REFUSAL TO GIVE ONE NUMBER IS THE FINDING - the walled bucket is 2.4x the dead bucket, so which side it is folded into changes the headline by 16 points.
answer_to_the_question.part_2_archival_fallback_for_dead_links: For the 24 dead/unreachable citations: 19 (79%) have SOME archive snapshot, 13 (54%) have a snapshot that CONTAINS the specific cited target, and 5 (21%) have no snapshot at all and are unrecoverable. So the answer to 'is there an archival snapshot that contains the quoted text' is YES for a bare majority (13/24) and NO or UNTESTABLE for the rest.
answer_to_the_question.part_3_the_premise_correction: The unit distinguishes itself from ADV-0080 by attacking DECAYED citations rather than FABRICATED ones. Measurement shows the boundary does not hold in practice: of 10 live-200 content mismatches, 1 is decay and 6 are targets that were never in the source, which is ADV-0080's class. A linkrot audit that does not run the archive comparison will mis-route 6 of 10 findings to the wrong remediation.

method_limitations_inline: UNVERIFIED: the walled 14.9% could contain dead pages. A 403 from a WAF is returned for live and dead paths alike on several hosts, so the dead rate is a LOWER BOUND.
The T1-ANCHOR check accepts a de-slugged phrase match as CONTAINS, which is deliberately permissive; it biases toward under-reporting anchor decay, not over-reporting it.

Archive snapshots were selected nearest to 20260718, but several nearest snapshots are months from that date (e.g. 20210318 for asrs.arc.nasa.gov), so 'predates the citation' is solid while 'reflects what the citing agent saw' is not.

This unit probed the network from one Windows host on one residential IP with one user-agent. Host-level blocking is IP- and UA-dependent, so the walled fraction is not portable to another vantage point.
report.probe_1_as_specified: SPEC: 'HTTP-resolve every URL and record status, final URL after redirects, and whether the quoted string appears in the fetched body.' DONE for 420 sampled urls (390 after purification): status, final_url, redirected flag, body_chars, containment verdict and detail are recorded per url in adv0020_probe1b.json results[]. DEVIATION disclosed: 'every URL' was reduced to a stratified sample of a 5,144-url frame because a full census at polite per-host rates does not fit the 5,400s budget; the command-center claim-record subset IS a full census.
report.probe_2_as_specified: SPEC: 'for non-200 or content-mismatch cases, query the archive by URL and timestamp and re-check the quoted string there.' DONE for all 52 non-200 + hard-target-mismatch urls: CDX index query, nearest-to-20260718 snapshot selection, raw /web/<ts>id_/ replay fetch, and the SAME containment check re-run inside the archived body. Mechanical independence from Probe 1: different host, different API surface, different data vintage, different failure mode. The first attempt at this probe was DISCARDED because its controls failed.
report.cross_reference_to_ADV_0080: not_a_duplicate_because says ADV-0080 attacks FABRICATED citations and this one attacks DECAYED ones. This unit hands ADV-0080 six concrete candidates it should adjudicate: the NEVER-CONTAINED set, where the cited anchor or phrase is absent from both today's page and a pre-citation archive snapshot. They are listed with their citing file in report.silent_failure_adjudication.
